title: Exact Strong Approximation Rates for CIR Processes
statement:
Let the Cox–Ingersoll–Ross process satisfy
$$
X_t=x+\int_0^t(a-bX_s)\,ds+\int_0^t\sigma\sqrt{X_s}\,dW_s,
$$
where $a,\sigma>0$ and $b,x\geq0$. For approximations of $X_T$ based on $N$ equidistant evaluations of $W$, is the optimal absolute-mean convergence order throughout the full parameter range equal to
$$
\min\left\{\frac{2a}{\sigma^2},1\right\}
$$?

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** For the Cox--Ingersoll--Ross strong-approximation problem, the conjectured rate is proved in boundary and other parameter regimes and matching lower bounds are known in parts, but the full exact-rate statement in the record is not established uniformly over all positive parameters.
